mechanism: Compute 2nd finite difference at sampling lag S (e.g. S=24 on H1 for daily cycle): Δ²_S ≈ x[t]−2x[t−S]+x[t−2S]. Near zero when a repeating cycle (any shape) or long-enough trend holds; sum of last S differences stays near zero under stable cycle/trend and diverges when a new cycle/trend starts—used as a disturbance/cycle-break detector. Adaptive MA level forms a discrete harmonic-oscillator residual.
data_needed: Price series; Sampling period matched to hypothesized cycle; optional adaptive MA level.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Forex symbols generally; H1 example with daily (24) sampling; Market Watch multi-symbol Slutsky demos
why_new_for_mis: Finite-difference residual and its rolling sum give MIS a cycle-stability vs cycle-break change sensor without assuming sinusoidal shape.
quote: If there is a cycle or cycles in the price movement, then the 2 nd difference will be zero. ... If there are any disturbances in the market (the beginning of a new trend, the launch of a new cycle, or the end of an old one), the sum of the differences will begin to deviate significantly.
